# Unit3 audit follow-up plan
Priority 1: strengthen week 1 retrieval for fixed/pre/post-test loops, primitive types/operators and complex Boolean precedence. Add explicit scope transfer and correct Python parameter-binding explanation. Use existing lesson practice allocation, not extra weeks.
Priority 2: compare all formal pseudocode and Cisco diagram conventions with current support references. Add/verify a worked Gantt exemplar and student schedule evidence. Do not label illustrative concept diagrams as verified Cisco symbols.
Priority 3: collect learner-designed tests, breakpoint evidence, representative environment/load/response observations, independent subnet/diagram work and authorised live ping/traceroute. Synthetic examples are retained as teaching aids, not proof of actual deployment.
Priority 4: independent teacher review of the mapping, answers, code and assessment outline. Confirm assessment percentages/conditions and class period contact hours. Four lessons × 16 weeks = 64 lessons, project 12 already embedded. At 55 minutes per lesson = 58 hours 40 minutes; at 50 minutes per lesson = 53 hours 20 minutes, requiring review against notional 55 hours per unit.
Priority 5: retain the published CC BY 4.0 licence for original textbook content and the MIT licence for original code. Check separately credited third-party material against its own reuse conditions. Teacher files are separate but publicly accessible.
Next work: verify formal conventions and collect practical evidence before claiming completion; Unit 4 draft chapters and a grouped audit are now available through Coverage & audits. Audit identifiers are local editorial groups, not official syllabus numbering.
